page: Amazon Web Services m8idn.xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. The hardware profile features an Intel x86_64 architecture processor running at 3.9 GHz, delivering 4 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory is configured at 16.0 GB, resulting in an exact 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include discrete GPU accelerators.

Integrated local storage is a defining characteristic of this instance type, which provides a bundled 237 GB direct-attached NVMe SSD. For data transfer, the instance is provisioned with a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps. While the local NVMe storage enables low-latency read and write operations, the instance store is ephemeral by design, meaning data does not persist across stop or termination cycles.

From an operational cost perspective, bundled NVMe storage provides high input/output performance for scratch space, temporary indexing, and caching without the need to allocate separate network-attached block volumes for those operations. The balanced compute, memory, and high-speed local disk configuration makes this server suited for database instances, memory-to-disk caching tiers, container hosts, and continuous integration build nodes.
description: Amazon Web Services m8idn.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the Nitro system and powered by a 3.9 GHz Intel x86_64 processor. The configuration delivers 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory distribution. It integrates a 237 GB direct-attached NVMe SSD for fast local read and write operations, alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps. Containing no discrete GPU acceleration, the hardware balances general computing requirements with high-speed local temporary storage. Utilizing the on-box NVMe volume reduces dependence on auxiliary network-attached storage for intermediate disk operations, though data persistence must be managed externally due to the storage medium's ephemeral nature. The m8idn.xlarge is suitable for transactional database nodes, caching systems, containerized web backends, and data processing pipelines.
